bottleneck: Minimal-genome chassis organisms promise clean, predictable platforms for biomanufacturing, but stripping genomes to essentials often yields fragile cells: slow growth, mutation accumulation, and loss of engineered functions over generations. Evolution relentlessly degrades synthetic constructs that impose metabolic burden, and the removed 'non-essential' genes often prove essential under industrial stress conditions. No chassis yet combines minimalism with industrial robustness, and each new product may need its own optimized host.
current_state: JCVI-syn3.0 and similar minimal cells are research tools, not production platforms. Industrial work still relies on heavily domesticated but genetically messy E. coli and yeast strains.
title: Minimal genome chassis lack industrial stability
why_it_blocks: Without stable minimal chassis, biomanufacturing stays locked to a few legacy organisms, limiting which chemistries and products synthetic biology can economically produce. The platform revolution stalls at the host-organism level.
